book_question: What is the Grace, really? (Book II; Darrow fights on his feet but cannot run: every fight held, not chased)

chapter.question: Can a company that will not run hold the crossing the ford was lost at, and what does the truth of that river cost the people who finally read it?

slots.plan: The afternoon of the weir. Open on his answer to the weir choice (or, if it is still open at the close, keep her fate to Monday's opening by the default rule). Maelis sews the sword arm on the cart's tail, brisk and dry (the Hard-won needle; the two fingers stay as they are, never healed), and the company's verdict on a man who won by not moving is wry and loud. The stick comes back: Ash, who does not fetch, goes down the bank below the fall and brings it up in her teeth, once; or Rae cuts him one from the millrace hazel. Then the bridge: upstream, the far-bank carts start to cross in a hurry, the millers come down from the mill, and a miller names the captain of the Ninth (c06.8b: he does not turn his head). Rae reads the line before he says it: carts behind, children shushed, everyone looking back, the shape of the clan line at the ford (thread 3). At dusk something moves at the field's edge across the river, slow, many, and nobody says the word (T4 plant).
slots.turn: Darrow sees the ford's shape drawn up on the far bank and, for once, is on the right side of a bridge to do something about it; the company decides with him that nobody sleeps.

slots.plan: The bridge held, the mirror of Harrow Ford, and this time he holds: the carts cross under the mill's lamps through the night while what came through the fields reaches the far end. Darrow stands the bridge as he stood the stone, sewn arm and all; Rae's cart is the barricade and she reads the line before he says it (rae.road). What holds in every tier is shown here: every cart crosses, and the mill burns (the fixed loss: how it goes up is the scene's; its price comes at Sunday's climax by the tier). The warmth comes the same night: the millers' bread at the burned mill, forty strangers and five of the company round one fire. The millers speak of an older ring of standing stone in the frozen marsh up the north road, which the mill-folk do not go near. Ends on b2.3's beat choice: the millers.
slots.turn: Darrow holds a crossing he could not hold at the ford, and is left at a burned mill with forty people who now look to him: he must decide what they are to him.

micro.ask: Forty millers at a burned mill, with the bridge behind them. What does Darrow do with them?
options: Keep them: the company goes on forty larger, at a cart's pace.
Send them up the Holloway to Saint Ysolde's with the House's name and Rae's word for the road.
Leave them at the mill with the company and follow the walkers' trail back west at first light, with Ash and nobody else, to find where four hundred of them came from.

slots.plan: Opens at first light at the burned mill, on his answer to the millers in a clause, and on the dawn: with the light the line on the bridge are walkers again and drift off east along the far bank; Rae takes her cart off the bridge; Maelis answers the woman's wrist (the tier is Sunday's: here only 'it is warmer than it was'). Then the slot's own matter: Hollis takes the paper out of the leg's cup at last, at the burned mill, and looks at the wax: the seal (thread 1 and thread 2 pay off here; the T3 reveal is on the page with its plants). The order to charge, into a river the Second had been told to hold. He reads it once and puts it away and says nothing that matters all day, which is the thing to fear. Callback c05.9b is not for this slot: its fit needs b2.4 under way, which this slot's own record makes true, so the brief offers it from Wednesday; fire it Thursday or Friday (the well, sober).
slots.turn: Hollis, who carried the order unread for a year, reads it; the company learns the old captain's quiet is worse than his noise.
slots.tone: grief and anger, plain and short

slots.plan: The Tether, stage 2 (a hand), re-skinned to the road: the cart's tail at dusk, away from the mill's smoke. Her palms: the rope-burn ridges, the crooked thumb; the cage, her father, the splice that went quiet before it went. A rope is softest where it is worn smooth, she says, which is the only thing she and Maelis have ever agreed on without knowing it. Then her question, a carter's, after the weir: why he does not take the fast road down and kneel and have it all back, when she would, if anyone offered it to carters. Ends on the micro. Closes with the Reckoning box line for the Tether.
slots.turn: Rae shows him a hurt she has never shown anyone and asks him the question nobody on his bank has asked; he must answer her, not a hunter.

micro.ask: Why not the fast road, then? Down, kneel, have it back. What does Darrow say?
options: "Because they'd hang me at the bottom of the Steps before I reached a stone."
Say nothing; show her the knee.

slots.plan: Hollis carries the read seal a day. The company goes round him rough and warm and talking, not silent: Maelis with work, Wren with a story he can correct, Rae with the oxen, each in their own way, and he lets them. He does not drink, or he does, and the page shows which. By evening he has the question ready and has not asked it. Callback c05.2a may fire (Rae has known since the inn what Darrow saw; she does not open what she carries). Shape A is confirmed: Knot IV tied Mon 11/16 (PT 15), inside the window, so nothing is re-planned at this close; the week runs as planned and Book II crosses at Sunday's climax.
slots.turn: The company holds Hollis up without being asked to; Darrow sees the question coming and knows he will have to choose how much of the ford to give him.

slots.plan: Hollis asks, sober (r.b2.hollis_sober is armed): what did the Captain see from the water? Darrow has the three heartbeats, the Second dry on its bank, the horse already turned, and since the weir what the rider said: everyone in the Second knew. Ends on b2.4's beat choice, never Saturday.
slots.turn: The one man who was under the order asks for the truth of it, and Darrow must decide how much of the ford a friend can carry.

micro.ask: Hollis asks what the Captain saw from the water. What does Darrow tell him?
options: All of it, at once, before Hollis has finished asking: the three heartbeats, the Second dry on its bank, the horse already turned when the order came.
The seal and the day, and not the heartbeat: spare him the one thing that cannot be unsaid.
All of it, and then the paper out of his hand and into the fire, so nobody will ever read that seal against the Sixth's captain again.

slots.plan: The road north to the ring the millers spoke of, a lead-in with no choice: the frozen marsh, the cold, the company smaller in the open. On the road Darrow opens the miller's letter at last, the one in the hand that was not Aldric's: Aldric does not sleep (q2.lantern's letter; its answer waits for another week). By dusk the ring is in sight across the reeds, older than Calden. Shape A confirmed (Knot IV tied Mon 11/16): this day stands as planned.
slots.turn: Darrow learns from the letter that the man he wants to face is not sleeping either, and walks toward an old ring he means to read.

invite.want: to see the script on his palms when it comes, what it looks like, and to be told first what it says at the ring
invite.why_now: tomorrow he means to read an old ring in the marsh, and she has watched the script come up on his hands all week without once being shown it
invite.if_ignored: she goes to the ring without asking, and keeps to the back with a lamp

world_moves: In the night the far-bank carts cross on their own, the millers bar the mill and light every lamp, and by morning the fields across the river are full of slow shapes standing at the edge of the light.
Riders in dark coats watch the mill bridge from the far ridge for an hour, then turn back south.
A Confessor's rider comes up the mill tracks with a new writ, and the bell-post at the fork carries a third paper.

climax.plan: Shape A (the Knot tied by Thu 11/19's close): The Stonewright Ruin (arc b2.5). A ring of broken Oathstone in a frozen marsh, older than Calden, by lamplight. Darrow reads what the Reckoning lets him; Wren finishes the line he cannot and does not say how (the first time her reading is on the page: openly if r.b2.wren_reads arms, caught at it if not). The script says what the stones are for (T1 and T2 confirmed). Maelis says, "Yes," and nothing else. The week's two beat outcomes land here by the tier beside the ring's (the bridge's price, Hollis's hour). Then the choice; once he answers, the crossing (t2) is its Choice block, and Book III opens with Ch 8. Shape B (not tied by then): b2.4's choice becomes this climax (Friday re-planned at Thursday's close), and b2.5 and the crossing are Ch 8's.
climax.tone: wonder first, then dread; the Book's one long silence
checks: resolve (Warden's Eye: reading the ring by lamplight, as far as the Reckoning lets him)
resolve (letting Wren finish the line without asking how)
vigor (the marsh at night: the cold, the lamps lit and kept)
options: Tell the company, all of it, at the ring, with Maelis's one word behind him.
Carry it alone until he knows what to do with it.
Tell them, and send it: the stones' words in his own hand down the Holloway by the Market's line, to every bell-house that will read it, before the Confessors can answer.

quest_summary: Confessor Ivo Marrant is coming up the Holloway with five grey cloaks (six in all), a cart, a censer, and a writ naming the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's. Darrow's name is first; Hollis is second. Rae Thorne, the carter who heard the list read, is in the House; her cart and oxen wait at the winch-house below, where one of the six will stay; the rest camp on the lower terrace under the gate.
